classification.difficultyReason: Find an exact radical stationary point and compare its function value with both endpoints.

content.prompt: Find the global minimum and maximum for $y=x^4-2x+1$ in the domain $[-2,3]$.

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrowheads at both ends; blue quartic with closed domain endpoints. Reconstructed from the printed equation.
spec.mathematics: y=x^4-2x+1 on [-2,3]; endpoints (-2,21) and (3,76); minimum at x=1/cuberoot(2).
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no answer coordinates or extrema labels.

answer.short: Global minimum at $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2}},1-\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt[3]{2}}\right)$; global maximum at $(3,76)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}y'&=4x^3-2\\4x^3-2&=0\\x^3&=\frac12\\x&=\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2}}\end{aligned}$$
This stationary point lies in the domain. Compare its value with the endpoint values:
$$\begin{aligned}y(-2)&=16+4+1=21\\y\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2}}\right)&=\frac{1}{2\sqrt[3]{2}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{2}}+1\\&=1-\frac{3}{2\sqrt[3]{2}}\\y(3)&=81-6+1=76\end{aligned}$$
The global minimum is $1-\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt[3]{2}}$ at $x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{2}}$. The global maximum is $76$ at $x=3$.
